chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Musa ibn Amir from Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said:

Two commanders, yet they are not two commanders: The bearer of the funeral (or the one leading the funeral procession) is not such that those following it may return before he gives them permission; and a woman who performed Hajj with a group of men fell ill with menstruation, so it is not for them to return and leave her until she gives them permission.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْجَنَازَةِ: The bearer of the funeral or the one leading the funeral procession

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a group leaving a funeral procession or a woman menstruating during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *tamakkun* (authority/control) in two distinct contexts: the funeral procession and the Hajj group. It establishes that the leader (or the one in charge) holds the right to permit departure, emphasizing communal cohesion and the legal status of the menstruating woman as remaining part of the group despite her ritual impurity.
